messages:
anya.dev: heads up — saw two customers hit runtime errors when bundling the SDK into edge functions. errors vary: some bundles end up with undici inlined, others lose fetch entirely. we should agree a recommended bundler config and maybe add runtime assertions.

sam.bryant: sounds familiar. current SDK does dynamic import('undici') in a node fallback. but several bundlers (esbuild/rollup) will eagerly include that module unless it's marked external/conditional.

mohit.k: can we use a tiny runtime probe that aborts early if the environment is obviously not Node? e.g. check for process.versions.node and not detect "Deno" etc. But bundlers can still include the import if they can statically analyze it. dynamic import usually helps but some build tools still chase it.

anya.dev: proposal: keep dynamic import for undici, and add a small runtime shim that throws a descriptive error if fetch is missing, pointing to our docs and to bundler externals config. Also produce a debug log when undici is loaded so ops know why it happened.

sam.bryant: +1. we should also ship a webpack/rollup/esbuild snippet in examples/ showing how to mark undici as external and how to polyfill only for server targets.

olivia.qa: on the QA side we've had flaky tests because jest-jsdom provides a fake fetch implementation missing streaming semantics. tests accidentally passed but prod failed. we need a test matrix that includes jsdom, node-global-fetch and undici so we catch behavior mismatch.

taylor_p: I can add a smoke test that runs with node16 (undici), node18 (global), and jsdom env. also add an assertion in our test harness that checks for 'isNativeFetchCompatible' helper to validate Response.prototype.text exists and that body is cloneable.

mohit.k: typing note: consumers using "lib.dom" will be fine, but our published d.ts should avoid referencing undici types directly. if we need helper types for internal adapters, keep them in a separate internal-only d.ts. Avoid leaking Undici types into public interfaces.

anya.dev: bundler checklist we should add to README: 1) if targeting browsers/workers, mark undici as external, 2) enable DOM lib in tsconfig (Request/Response types), 3) for server-only bundles, add undici to dependencies and allow dynamic import, 4) document runtime error message and link to troubleshooting.

sam.bryant: about retries and bodies — reiterating: streamed bodies are not cloneable across all runtimes. solution: buffer bodies up to a configurable limit for automatic retries, otherwise mark request non-retriable. add a small helper BufferBody.from(body) that returns a cloneable representation.

olivia.qa: test matrix action item: include an integration scenario with a small image upload (stream) and verify SDK does not attempt automatic retry for that route, plus a small JSON payload that is retriable and gets buffered.

ci-bot: GH actions: added new job 'runtime-compat' with matrix: node16,node18,bun-minor,jsdom. Added miniflare smoke test for workers.

anya.dev: logging/telemetry: emit 'fetch_runtime_notice' event the first time SDK chooses fallback to undici with tags {runtime, reason}. redact any host headers or URIs.

sam.bryant: docs PR checklist: add examples/bundler-configs, runtime-detection.md, and a small code sample that shows how to opt into a custom fetch (for customers who prefer to pass their own).

anya.dev: sample to include in README for custom fetch:
```js
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference';
import crossFetch from 'cross-fetch';

const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, fetch: crossFetch });
```

sam.bryant: good. also mention that passing your own fetch bypasses our telemetry for runtime selection but still runs our retry wrapper — document implications for Request cloning.

mohit.k: action items: taylor -> PR runtime probe + adapter; sam -> examples and logging; anya -> docs and troubleshooting; olivia -> add tests for streaming vs buffered bodies.

anya.dev: thanks team. target: land before next patch. will follow up with RFC draft for the new public typings and the bundle guidance. :rocket:
